🔊 Netanyahu calls for Zionist unity to eliminate Iran — as election deadlock leaves him scrambling
With the votes counting and no clear path to a majority, Benjamin Netanyahu is rejecting any reliance on Arab parties and demanding the right-wing bloc unite to form a government — and to go to war with Iran.
"The Zionist majority must come to its senses and unite... Israel has a once-in-a-lifetime historic opportunity, together with President Trump, to eliminate the existential Iranian threat," he declared.
Exit polls show Netanyahu’s bloc at 50-52 seats — far short of the 61 needed. Nevertheless, Likud will remain the largest party in the Knesset, which gives Netanyahu significant leverage in forming a government.

🔊 Eisenkot to Netanyahu: 'Do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs!'
With Israel facing a deadlocked election, opposition leader and former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot issued a stark public warning to Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of trying to drag the country into war to save his political career.
Eisenkot also addressed the defense establishment, warning them against following Netanyahu's hawkish policy of maintaining power through killing and bombing.
"Netanyahu is a transitional prime minister, without a mandate and without trust. Remember that you serve the state and the interests of the citizens of Israel alone. Stand strong and steadfast against any attempt to challenge you. You have my clear backing."

⚔️🇮🇷 Iran's Supreme Leader calls for an end to war and stronger regional security
Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has called for securing Tehran's terms to end the war with the US and Israel, warning against allowing the country to remain trapped in a state of “neither war nor peace.”
Meeting with Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei, Khamenei insisted that any settlement must protect Iran's interests and those of the Resistance Front.
The talks also addressed Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, regional security, and closer cooperation with neighboring countries.
Khamenei credited Iran's resistance with putting its adversaries under pressure and called for stronger national unity, while Rezaei outlined plans for regional security arrangements built around the region's own countries.
